conceptBeforeSelection: Crime, justice and behavioural evidence: investigate crime and social responses through criminal-law reasoning, psychosocial explanations, prevention and empiricalresearch. Thistargetconnection ismorethan a general socialscience theme.
programmeJudgment: Promising substantive response through actual criminal law, criminological research, extremism prevention, racialised punishment, aggression, development and empirical methods. These are concrete contributions, beyond general social-science coherence. The missing revised external third year prevents final comparability. General psychology or networking does not establish victimology, policing, penology or cybercrime progression. No academic no-match is approved.
candidateStopping: No accepted alternative yet: the first-comparison gate depends on the external curriculum. Policy/inequality and cybercrime directions remain distinct candidate tests. Additional accepted programmes would need substantive distinctness and the30EC/four-course floor. Do not fill three slots by arbitrary substitutions.

courses.name: Personal & Professional Development
courses.judgment: Year-1 PPD develops academic writing, research literacy and community collaboration, relevant to the skill labs and introductory research. It does not itself supply crime theory.

courses.name: Law, Society & Justice
courses.judgment: Legal and sociolegal foundations include criminal, administrative, constitutional, tort and human-rights law, social control, race/gender, IRAC and mock trials. Strong partial foundation; broader than Dutch criminology law.

courses.name: Human Rights: Law & Philosophy
courses.judgment: Human-rights inquiry includes torture, punishment and dignity. Concrete legal and normative complement, without full criminal procedure.

courses.name: Criminal Law & Criminal Justice
courses.judgment: Criminal liability, criminalisation, punishment and a simulated legal clinic combine with an actual criminology or organised-crime research proposal. Strong subject response beyond a title match; not the complete policing, victimology or cybercrime curriculum.

courses.name: Comparative Constitutional Law
courses.judgment: Administrative discretion, procedural fairness, remedies and judicial review support governance and legal-protection questions. Comparative rather than specifically Dutch criminal enforcement.

courses.name: Introduction to Sociology
courses.judgment: Socialisation, groups, stratification, race/class and sociological case analysis support inequality and social explanations of crime. No claim that every case concerns crime.

courses.name: Qualitative Research Methodology
courses.judgment: Actual interviews, observation, document coding, ethics and team empirical research directly respond to the qualitative methods. Different software does not invalidate the academic relationship.

courses.name: Modern Sociology
courses.judgment: Functionalism, symbolic interactionism, stigma, critical theory and power support explanation and social construction of deviance. Not a full criminological-theory sequence.

courses.name: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory
courses.judgment: Trust, solidarity, civil repair and public spheres provide specific institutional complements. Civil-society research is not automatically crime prevention.

courses.name: Public Policy Analysis
courses.judgment: Description-only policy cycles, globalisation, a sugar case and policy memos receive full consideration. They support policy reasoning but do not establish criminal-policy cost-benefit analysis.

courses.name: Ethics
courses.judgment: Utilitarian, deontological and other ethical arguments support moral and punishment reasoning. This is not empirical penology.

courses.name: Introduction to Brain & Behavior
courses.judgment: Learning, personality, social influence, neural mechanisms and mental disorders support psychological foundations. No unsupported claim about biological crime causation.

courses.name: Social Psychology
courses.judgment: Aggression, prejudice, social cognition, group influence and empirical design support behavioural explanations. The project proposes a study rather than conducting one.

courses.name: Statistics & Experimental Methods
courses.judgment: Substantial experimental design, ANOVA, multivariable analysis and R/SPSS work respond to quantitative research and experiments. Crime datasets are not required by this UCR course.

courses.name: Psychopathology
courses.judgment: Actual forensic-psychology content, personality/substance disorders, stigma and biopsychosocial causation are meaningful connections. Do not equate mental illness with crime or claim complete forensic training.

courses.name: Psychodiagnostics & Psychotherapies
courses.judgment: Reliability, validity, clinical interviewing, diagnostic evidence and treatment assessment support critical assessment. Clinical work is not eyewitness interrogation or criminal rehabilitation itself.

courses.name: Advanced Research Methods & Statistics
courses.judgment: Systematic reviews, meta-analysis, R, effects and bias strongly support evidence synthesis. A criminological application requires an actual supported focus; no original field experiment claimed.

courses.name: Lifespan Developmental Psychology
courses.judgment: Developmental risk and protection, adolescence, attachment and life-course analysis support offender-development questions. The actual interview involves an adult over50, not juvenile-offender fieldwork.

courses.name: Youth Resilience to Extremism
courses.judgment: Actual radicalisation, violent extremism, terrorism, psychosocial risks/protection and educational prevention are direct subject connections. Research is translated into a toolkit and revised using recipient feedback.

courses.name: Philosophy of Mind
courses.judgment: Mind, self and perception provide a bounded conceptual complement. Eyewitness reliability is not specified.

courses.name: Philosophy of Emotion
courses.judgment: Moral and political emotions, fear, anger and decision-making deepen affective/social interpretation. Philosophical inquiry is not empirical forensic evidence.

courses.name: Free Will, Time & the Self
courses.judgment: Actual agency, moral responsibility, determinism, addiction and luck complement questions of criminal responsibility. Not a substitute for criminal-liability doctrine.

courses.name: Perception & Action
courses.judgment: Description-only sensory processing and goal-directed action receive full consideration as cognitive foundations. No recognition-procedure or lie-detection instruction inferred.

courses.name: Higher Order Functions
courses.judgment: Attention, memory, cognitive control, social cognition and experimental design provide concrete foundations for evidence and decision bias. A criminal-witness application is not guaranteed.

courses.name: Introduction to Programming
courses.judgment: Actual Python and computational problem-solving support digital analysis tools. They do not teach cybercrime causes or investigation.

courses.name: Introduction to Data Science
courses.judgment: R, text/spatial data, cleaning and visualisation support quantitative patterns and environmental analysis. The chosen research question need not concern crime.

courses.name: Machine Learning
courses.judgment: Prediction, classification, validation and feature engineering support evaluation of predictive models. Actual policing models or criminal-network cases are not specified.

courses.name: AI Ethics
courses.judgment: Actual forensic-psychology AI applications, privacy, surveillance, fairness and responsibility support digital-justice questions. No full cybercrime or evidence sequence inferred.

courses.name: Networks & Operating Systems
courses.judgment: Networks, operating systems and Wireshark investigation provide relevant infrastructure and packet-analysis methods. No documented malware, offending or law-enforcement curriculum.

courses.name: Database Management Systems
courses.judgment: Description-only SQL, relational theory, authorisation and query processing receive full consideration. Database foundations do not establish cybercriminology.

courses.name: Introduction to Economics
courses.judgment: Rational choice, game theory, costs and market foundations support economic explanations. Crime-control cost-benefit evaluation itself is not specified.

courses.name: International Macroeconomics
courses.judgment: Macroeconomic, labour and policy content gives social context; it is a less direct response to criminal policy and offending.

courses.name: Microeconomics & Behavior
courses.judgment: Choice under uncertainty, cognitive limitations, efficiency, externalities and government provide behavioural/economic tools. Not criminal-policy evaluation; BENGATE102 required.

courses.name: Psychology of Leading Under Pressure
courses.judgment: Minority experience, emotion, identity safety and a substantive ethical survey project offer relevant behavioural/inequality methods. Leadership is not criminological intervention; BENGATE102 required.

courses.name: Social Movements & Environmental Justice
courses.judgment: Description-only social movements and environmental-justice cases receive full consideration. Environmental justice does not establish the spatial study of offending.

courses.name: Media & Race
courses.judgment: Actual crime, punishment, the racialised body, incarceration, extremist propaganda and archival/observational methods offer concrete historical connections to criminalisation and communities. American focus; not Dutch procedure.
